items.q: What is Just 7?
items.a: A laundry detergent sheet made with seven ingredients. Drop one in the drum, it's designed to dissolve,† and your clothes get clean. No jug, no measuring cup, no mystery list.

items.q: What are laundry detergent sheets?
items.a: Thin, dry sheets of concentrated detergent. They do the job of liquid detergent without the heavy plastic jug, and they're light to ship and easy to store.

items.q: Why is it called Just Seven?
items.a: Because that's the whole list: seven ingredients, counting the sheet itself. Just Seven is the brand, Just 7 is the first sheet. The naming story.

items.q: What's the difference between Just Seven and Just 7?
items.a: Just Seven is the company. Just 7 is our first product, the everyday laundry sheet.

items.q: Is it Just 7 or Just Seven sheets?
items.a: Either works when you're searching. The product on the pouch is Just 7.

items.q: Who is Just 7 for?
items.a: Anyone who wants a short, readable label on their laundry: fragrance-free homes, vegan households, people with pets, and anyone tired of hauling jugs.

items.q: What does Just 7 do best?
items.a: Everyday loads: clothes, sheets, towels and pet bedding with normal grime. Heavy protein stains need a pretreat.

items.q: Is Just 7 a laundry detergent or a softener?
items.a: A detergent. It cleans. It isn't a fabric softener or a dryer sheet.

items.q: Is Just 7 a dryer sheet?
items.a: No. It goes in the washer, not the dryer. It's detergent in sheet form.

items.q: Do laundry sheets actually work?
items.a: Sheets use the same kinds of cleaners as liquid detergent, just dried into a film. Independent testers have found many sheets weaker than top liquids on hard stains, so we won't make a performance claim until our own side-by-side test is done.†

items.q: Are laundry sheets a scam?
items.a: No, they're a real detergent format. Results vary by formula, so read the ingredient list and the dosing guide, and buy from the brand's own site.

items.q: Are laundry detergent sheets worth it?
items.a: If you value a light pouch, no measuring and a short label, yes. If you mostly wash heavily stained loads, plan to pretreat.

items.q: Is Just 7 eco-friendly?

items.q: What are the 7 ingredients in Just 7?
items.a: Pullulan film, lauryl glucoside, decyl glucoside, sodium carbonate (washing soda), plant glycerin, sodium citrate and water. Every one explained.

items.q: Why only seven ingredients?
items.a: We kept only what a sheet has to do: clean, soften the water and hold together. If we can't explain an ingredient in one sentence, it's out. The case for a short label.

items.q: Does fewer ingredients mean it cleans less?
items.a: Not for everyday loads. Longer lists often add enzymes, fillers and fragrance. Enzymes help with heavy protein stains, so pretreat those or wait for Just 9.†

items.q: Are fewer ingredients always better?
items.a: Not automatically. Every ingredient should earn its place, and a short list makes that easy to check.

items.q: Why do you count the film as an ingredient?
items.a: Because it goes into your washer with everything else. Counting it keeps comparisons fair.

items.q: Why is water on the ingredient list?
items.a: It's in the recipe while the sheet is made, and most of it dries off. We count everything, so it's listed.

items.q: What is Just 7 made from?
items.a: A pullulan film made from fermented starch, two glucoside cleaners, washing soda, Plant glycerin, sodium citrate and water. Nothing from animals.

items.q: Are the ingredient percentages final?
items.a: They're our working formula. We'll confirm the final numbers with our manufacturer's documents before launch and match the pouch exactly.†

items.q: How much does one sheet weigh?
items.a: Roughly 2 g in our working formula.†

items.q: What's the ingredient breakdown by percent?
items.a: Working formula: pullulan film 35%, lauryl glucoside 17%, decyl glucoside 17%, sodium carbonate 10%, plant glycerin 10%, sodium citrate 7%, water 4%.†

items.q: Where can I see the full ingredient label?
items.a: On our ingredients page and the product page.

items.q: What's in laundry detergent sheets in general?
items.a: Usually cleaners (surfactants), water softeners, a film to hold it together, and often fragrance, enzymes or preservatives. What's in laundry sheets.

items.q: What does a surfactant do?
items.a: It lets water grab oil and dirt so they rinse away. Ours are lauryl glucoside and decyl glucoside.

items.q: What is pullulan?
items.a: A film made from fermented starch. It's the same family of material used in dissolving breath strips and some capsules. We use it instead of PVA.

items.q: What does pullulan film do in Just 7?
items.a: It holds everything in a thin, dry sheet, then is designed to dissolve in the wash.†

items.q: How is pullulan made?
items.a: A microbe feeds on starch, such as tapioca or corn, and makes pullulan through fermentation.

items.q: Is pullulan the same as PVA?
items.a: No. Pullulan comes from fermentation. PVA (polyvinyl alcohol) is a synthetic polymer.

items.q: Is pullulan a plastic?
items.a: Pullulan is a polysaccharide made by fermentation, not a synthetic polymer like PVA. We'll call the sheet plastic-free once the film spec is confirmed in writing.†

items.q: Where else is pullulan used?
items.a: Dissolving breath strips and some capsules use the same family of film.

items.q: How much of a sheet is pullulan?
items.a: About 35% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Does pullulan dissolve in cold water?
items.a: Just 7 is designed to dissolve in warm or cold water. We're running our own cold-water test and will share it.†

items.q: Is the pullulan from corn or tapioca?
items.a: Pullulan is made from fermented starch such as tapioca or corn. We'll name the confirmed starch source with the final film spec.

items.q: What is lauryl glucoside?
items.a: A cleaner that goes after body oils and grease, with a little lather. More on lauryl glucoside.

items.q: Is lauryl glucoside a sulfate?
items.a: No. It sounds like sodium lauryl sulfate, but it's a sugar-based cleaner, not a sulfate.

items.q: Where does lauryl glucoside come from?
items.a: It's a sugar-based cleaner. We'll share the supplier source when it's confirmed.†

items.q: Why use both lauryl and decyl glucoside?
items.a: They're from the same sugar-based family. Decyl is the gentle everyday cleaner and lauryl adds more grease-lifting muscle.

items.q: How much lauryl glucoside is in a sheet?
items.a: About 17% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Is lauryl glucoside the same as SLS?
items.a: No. Sodium lauryl sulfate is a sulfate. Lauryl glucoside is a glucoside made from sugar and a fatty alcohol.

items.q: What is decyl glucoside?
items.a: Our main everyday cleaner. It grabs oil and dirt and lets the water carry them away. More on decyl glucoside.

items.q: Where does decyl glucoside come from?
items.a: It's a sugar-based cleaner. We'll share the supplier source when it's confirmed.†

items.q: Is decyl glucoside ethoxylated?
items.a: No. It's made without ethoxylation. What ethoxylated means.

items.q: Why is decyl glucoside used in personal care?
items.a: It's known as one of the milder cleaners, which is why it shows up in many face washes and shampoos.

items.q: How much decyl glucoside is in a sheet?
items.a: About 17% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: What is sodium carbonate?
items.a: Washing soda. It raises the pH and softens water so everyday grime lets go more easily. More on washing soda.

items.q: Is sodium carbonate the same as baking soda?
items.a: No. Baking soda is sodium bicarbonate. Washing soda is sodium carbonate, which is stronger at softening water.

items.q: Where does sodium carbonate come from?
items.a: It's a mineral, made from salt and limestone or mined from trona ore.

items.q: Why is washing soda in Just 7?
items.a: It helps the cleaners work, especially in hard water. Laundry has used it for generations.

items.q: How much sodium carbonate is in a sheet?
items.a: About 10% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Is sodium carbonate the same as soda ash?
items.a: Yes, soda ash is another name for sodium carbonate.

items.q: What is plant glycerin?
items.a: It keeps the sheet soft and bendy so it doesn't crack in the pouch. More on plant glycerin.

items.q: Where does your glycerin come from?
items.a: It isn't from animals. We'll share the supplier spec when we have it.†

items.q: Why does it matter where glycerin comes from?
items.a: Glycerin can be made from animal fat, and labels usually don't say. Ours isn't from animals.†

items.q: Is the glycerin in Just 7 vegan?
items.a: Yes. Nothing in Just 7 comes from animals.†

items.q: How much glycerin is in a sheet?
items.a: About 10% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Does glycerin leave clothes greasy?
items.a: No. It's a small amount that keeps the sheet flexible, and it rinses away in the wash.

items.q: What is sodium citrate?
items.a: A water softener that helps the cleaners work and keeps the pH steady. More on sodium citrate.

items.q: Where does sodium citrate come from?
items.a: Citric acid from fermented sugar, paired with sodium.

items.q: Is sodium citrate a phosphate replacement?
items.a: Yes. It's a classic swap for the phosphates detergents used to use to soften water.

items.q: How much sodium citrate is in a sheet?
items.a: About 7% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Is sodium citrate food-grade?
items.a: Sodium citrate is used as a food ingredient, and it's a simple, well-known water softener.

items.q: What kind of water is in Just 7?
items.a: Purified water. It carries everything while the sheet is made, and most of it dries off.

items.q: How much water is in a sheet?
items.a: About 4% of a sheet in our working formula.†

items.q: Which ingredient does the cleaning?
items.a: Decyl glucoside and lauryl glucoside are the cleaners. Washing soda and sodium citrate help them by softening the water.

items.q: Which ingredients soften hard water?
items.a: Sodium carbonate and sodium citrate. They grab minerals so the cleaners can work.

items.q: Are any of the ingredients synthetic?
items.a: Each one is made through processing, like any detergent ingredient. We list the source of every one on our ingredients page.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain palm oil?
items.a: The fatty alcohol in our glucosides may come from coconut or palm. We'll name the confirmed source before launch.†

items.q: Does Just 7 contain coconut?
items.a: Our glucoside cleaners may use a fatty alcohol from coconut or palm. If you have a coconut allergy, ask your doctor and check the final label.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain corn?
items.a: Corn may be a source for the pullulan film and the sugar in our glucosides. We'll confirm sources on the final label.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain soy?
items.a: Soy oil is one possible source for our plant glycerin. We'll confirm the source before launch.

items.q: Is Just 7 gluten-free?
items.a: None of our seven ingredients is wheat, barley or rye, but we haven't tested for gluten, so we don't make that claim.

items.q: Do you have a safety data sheet?
items.a: We'll publish documents from our manufacturer before launch. Need one sooner for work? Contact us.

items.q: Can I get the ingredient list to show my doctor?
items.a: Yes. Print our ingredients page, or ask us for the full list by email.

items.q: Will the formula ever change?
items.a: If it does, we'll update the label and this page first. The name means seven, so the list stays short.

items.q: How do I read a laundry detergent label?
items.a: Look for a full ingredient list with what each one does. Read a label in 60 seconds.

items.q: What is GLDA?
items.a: A water softener planned for Just 9, not Just 7. What is GLDA.

items.q: Do any of the ingredients come from animals?
items.a: No. Nothing in Just 7 comes from animals. Washing soda is a mineral, and the rest of the list is on the ingredients page.

items.q: What pH is Just 7?
items.a: Washing soda makes it mildly alkaline, like most laundry detergents. We'll publish the measured pH from our manufacturer's documents before launch.

items.q: Is Just 7 concentrated?
items.a: Yes. It's a dry sheet with no water to ship, roughly 2 g each.†

items.q: What's the difference between a cleaner and a water softener?
items.a: Cleaners (our two glucosides) lift oil and dirt. Water softeners (sodium citrate and washing soda) tie up hard-water minerals so the cleaners can work.

items.q: Why isn't oxygen bleach in the sheet?
items.a: Most loads don't need it, and it would add to the list. Add oxygen bleach yourself when whites need a boost.

items.q: Will the pouch label match this site?
items.a: Yes. The final label will list the same seven ingredients, and we'll update this site if anything changes.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain fragrance?
items.a: No. Just 7 is fragrance-free, not just unscented. Why we skip fragrance.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain essential oils?
items.a: No, not even lavender. Why we never use essential oils.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain musks?
items.a: No. Nothing with musk in it, ever. Why we're musk-free.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain dyes?
items.a: No dyes. Your laundry doesn't need to be blue. Why no dyes.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain optical brighteners?
items.a: No. They're not on the list, and the list is the whole formula. Why we leave them out.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain sulfates?
items.a: No. Our cleaners are sugar-based glucosides, not sulfates.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain SLS or SLES?
items.a: No. Neither sodium lauryl sulfate nor sodium laureth sulfate is in Just 7.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain enzymes?
items.a: No. Enzymes help with heavy stains, but everyday loads often don't need them. Just 9 is planned to add them. Enzymes explained.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain PVA?
items.a: No. Our film is pullulan, not polyvinyl alcohol.†

items.q: Does Just 7 contain phosphates?
items.a: No. Sodium citrate and washing soda soften the water instead.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain bleach?
items.a: No chlorine bleach and no oxygen bleach. Chlorine vs oxygen bleach.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain parabens?
items.a: No. Parabens aren't among our seven ingredients.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain preservatives?
items.a: No added preservatives. Dry formats need fewer. Why dry formats need fewer.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain methylisothiazolinone (MIT)?
items.a: No. It's a preservative, and Just 7 has none on its list.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain 1,4-dioxane?
items.a: None of our seven ingredients is ethoxylated, the process linked to 1,4-dioxane. We haven't tested for trace contaminants, so we don't make a dioxane-free claim. What is 1,4-dioxane.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain ethoxylated ingredients?
items.a: No. Our glucoside cleaners aren't ethoxylated. What ethoxylated means.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain silicones?
items.a: No. Silicones in laundry products.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain clay or fillers?
items.a: No. Nothing added just for bulk. Why some detergents have clay.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain borax?
items.a: No. Borax isn't on our list.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain ammonia?
items.a: No.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain formaldehyde?
items.a: No formaldehyde and no formaldehyde-releasing preservatives on our list.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain phthalates?
items.a: No. Phthalates usually ride along with fragrance, and we use none.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain fabric softener?
items.a: No softeners or quats. It's a detergent only. Do you need fabric softener?.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain quats?
items.a: No. Quaternary ammonium compounds, common in softeners, aren't on our list.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain microplastics?
items.a: Our film is pullulan, not plastic, and it's designed to dissolve in the wash. We'll back that up with test data.†

items.q: Does Just 7 contain masking fragrance?
items.a: No. Some unscented products use a masking scent. We use none.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain animal ingredients?
items.a: No. Nothing from animals, including the glycerin.†

items.q: Does Just 7 contain lanolin?
items.a: No.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain tallow?
items.a: No. Tallow is animal fat, and nothing in Just 7 comes from animals.†

items.q: Does Just 7 contain hydrogen peroxide?
items.a: No.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain EDTA?
items.a: No. Sodium citrate softens our water instead.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain benzisothiazolinone?
items.a: No. Just 7 has no preservatives on its list.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain alcohol?
items.a: No ethanol. Lauryl and decyl glucoside are made with fatty alcohols, which are different from drinking alcohol.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain latex?
items.a: Latex isn't among our seven ingredients.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain nuts?
items.a: No nut ingredients. The glucoside fatty alcohols may come from coconut, which some allergy lists include. Check with your doctor.

items.q: Does Just 7 contain BPA?
items.a: BPA isn't one of our ingredients. We'll confirm the pouch material in writing before launch.

items.q: Why don't you add enzymes?
items.a: To keep the list short for everyday loads. Enzymes come in Just 9, planned for tough stains.

items.q: Why no optical brighteners?
items.a: They coat fabric to make it look brighter rather than cleaning it, and many people with sensitive skin avoid them.

items.q: Why no preservatives?
items.a: A dry sheet doesn't hold the water that liquid detergents do, so it doesn't need them.

items.q: Why no essential oils, even natural ones?
items.a: Many essential oils, lavender included, are a concern for cats. Fragrance-free also means nothing lingers on bedding.

items.q: What is the full list of things Just 7 leaves out?
items.a: PVA film, fragrance, essential oils, musks, dyes, sulfates, clay and fillers, and anything from animals.†

items.q: Is Just 7 free and clear?
items.a: It's fragrance-free with no dyes. "Free and clear" isn't a regulated term. What free and clear means.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for sensitive skin?
items.a: We can't promise how anyone's skin will react, but you can check every ingredient: seven, no fragrance, no dyes, no essential oils. If you have a skin condition, ask your doctor. Label guide for sensitive skin.

items.q: Is Just 7 hypoallergenic?
items.a: We don't use that word yet. There's no official standard for it, and we'd want patch testing first. Why we don't say it yet.†

items.q: Is Just 7 dermatologist tested?
items.a: Not yet, so we don't say it. What dermatologist tested means.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for eczema?
items.a: We make no medical claims. It's fragrance-free and dye-free with seven named ingredients, which makes it easy to check with your doctor.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for psoriasis?
items.a: We can't make medical claims. Share our seven-ingredient list with your dermatologist to decide.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for allergies?
items.a: We can't promise anything about allergies. What we can do is name every ingredient so you can check it against yours.

items.q: What's the difference between fragrance-free and unscented?
items.a: Unscented products can contain a masking fragrance to cover chemical smells. Fragrance-free means none at all, which is what Just 7 is. Full explainer.

items.q: Why choose fragrance-free laundry detergent?
items.a: Scent can linger on fabric and bedding. Fragrance-free leaves nothing behind but clean.

items.q: Will my clothes smell clean without fragrance?
items.a: Clean laundry smells like nothing. Without perfume, any smell left means the dirt is still there, so you know when to rewash.

items.q: Can I add my own scent to Just 7 laundry?
items.a: You can, but it won't be fragrance-free anymore. If you want scent, add it separately rather than mixing anything into the sheets.

items.q: Does Just 7 leave a scent on clothes?
items.a: No. Nothing is added to leave a scent.

items.q: Will Just 7 remove fragrance from previous detergents?
items.a: Repeated washes help. Heavy fragrance can take a few cycles to fade, and an extra rinse can help.

items.q: How do I switch to fragrance-free laundry?
items.a: Start with your bedding and towels, use the right dose, and add an extra rinse the first few washes to clear leftover scent.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for people with fragrance sensitivity?
items.a: It has no fragrance, no essential oils and no musks. Talk to your doctor about your specific sensitivity.

items.q: Does Just 7 trigger migraines?
items.a: We can't make medical claims. It has no fragrance, which many people who react to scent look for.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for asthma households?
items.a: We can't make medical claims. It's fragrance-free, so no perfume is added to the air or your laundry.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 on baby clothes?
items.a: Many parents look for short, fragrance-free labels for baby laundry, and Just 7 is one. Check with your pediatrician if your baby has sensitive skin. Washing baby clothes.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for newborn laundry?
items.a: Wash new baby clothes before first wear with the regular dose and an extra rinse. Ask your pediatrician about any skin concerns.

items.q: Do I need a separate baby detergent?
items.a: Not necessarily. Many parents choose one fragrance-free detergent for the whole home. Check with your pediatrician.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for kids' school uniforms?
items.a: Yes. Use one sheet for regular loads and pretreat grass and food stains first.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for sensitive skin and pets in the same home?
items.a: It's fragrance-free with no essential oils, which makes it a simple pick for both. Keep the pouch out of reach of kids and pets.

items.q: Does Just 7 have dyes that can irritate skin?
items.a: Just 7 has no dyes at all.

items.q: Can detergent residue cause itching?
items.a: Leftover detergent from overdosing can be an issue for some people. Use the right dose, don't overload, and add an extra rinse if you're unsure.

items.q: How do I avoid detergent residue?
items.a: Use the dosing guide, don't overstuff the drum, and add an extra rinse for heavy loads. Extra rinse explained.

items.q: Should I do an extra rinse for sensitive skin?
items.a: An extra rinse is an easy way to remove any leftover detergent. It's worth trying if you're sensitive.

items.q: I'm sensitive to one of the ingredients. What should I do?
items.a: Skip it, and please tell us which one. That's the point of a seven-name list: you can tell in ten seconds.

items.q: Can I patch test Just 7?
items.a: You can wash a single item first, like a pillowcase, and see how it goes before switching fully.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for underwear?
items.a: Yes. A half sheet works for a small load of underwear and delicates.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for face towels and pillowcases?
items.a: Yes. These touch your face most, which is why many people choose fragrance-free for them.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for cloth face masks?
items.a: Yes. Wash them like other everyday cotton items.

items.q: Will Just 7 irritate my skin?
items.a: We can't promise how your skin will react. You can check all seven ingredients and talk to your doctor.

items.q: Is Just 7 recommended by the National Eczema Association?
items.a: No. We don't have that seal and won't imply we do.

items.q: Is Just 7 EPA Safer Choice certified?
items.a: No, we don't have that certification. Safer Choice explained.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for sensitive skin and hard water at the same time?
items.a: Yes. Two of the seven ingredients soften hard water, and there's no fragrance or dye.

items.q: Does fragrance-free mean chemical-free?
items.a: No. Everything is a chemical, including water. Fragrance-free means no added scent.

items.q: What does "free and clear" mean?
items.a: Usually no fragrance and no dyes, but it isn't a regulated term. Free and clear explained.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for hospital scrubs or work uniforms?
items.a: Yes for everyday wear. Follow your employer's laundering rules for anything that needs disinfection.

items.q: Does Just 7 disinfect or sanitize?
items.a: No. Just 7 is a detergent, not a disinfectant. We make no germ-killing claims.

items.q: Does Just 7 kill dust mites?
items.a: We make no such claim. Hot washes are what people usually use for that; check your fabric's care label.

items.q: Is Just 7 good for pollen season?
items.a: Yes. Washing bedding and outerwear more often helps. Pollen season laundry tips.

items.q: Can people with chemical sensitivity use Just 7?
items.a: We can't make medical claims. It's fragrance-free with seven named ingredients for you to review.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 for breastfeeding or nursing clothes?
items.a: Yes. Wash nursing bras and burp cloths like other everyday laundry.

items.q: Will fragrance-free laundry still smell fresh after line drying?
items.a: Line-dried laundry picks up whatever is in the air but no perfume from us. Many people love that plain clean smell.

items.q: Can I wash bedding with Just 7 after getting a tattoo?
items.a: Fresh, clean bedding is part of most aftercare advice. We make no medical claims, so follow your artist's instructions.

items.q: How many sheets per load?
items.a: Half a sheet for a small load, one for a regular load, two for a big or extra-dirty load.† Dosing guide.

items.q: Where do I put the laundry sheet?
items.a: Straight into the drum, before your clothes. Not the detergent drawer.

items.q: Can I put the sheet in the detergent drawer?
items.a: No. Put it in the drum first, then add clothes.

items.q: Do I put the sheet on top of the clothes or under?
items.a: Under: sheet in the drum first, clothes on top.

items.q: How do I use laundry detergent sheets?
items.a: Drop a sheet in the empty drum, add clothes, wash. Use sheets in any washer.

items.q: Can I tear a sheet in half?
items.a: Yes. Half a sheet is the dose for a small load.

items.q: Can I cut a sheet with scissors?
items.a: Yes, though it tears cleanly by hand.

items.q: What counts as a small load?
items.a: Roughly a quarter to a third of the drum, like a few shirts or a set of workout clothes. Use half a sheet.

items.q: What counts as a regular load?
items.a: About half to two-thirds of the drum. Use one sheet.

items.q: What counts as a large load?
items.a: A full drum, bulky bedding or very dirty items. Use two sheets.

items.q: Do I need two sheets for a big load?
items.a: Yes, two sheets for big or extra-dirty loads.†

items.q: Can I use three sheets?
items.a: We don't recommend it. Two is our max for a load. Overdosing can leave residue.

items.q: What happens if I use too much detergent?
items.a: Extra detergent can leave residue and make fabrics feel stiff. Stick to the dosing guide.

items.q: What happens if I use too little?
items.a: Clothes may come out less clean, especially very soiled ones. Bump up to the next dose.

items.q: What temperature should I wash with?
items.a: Warm or cold, any normal cycle.† Follow your clothes' care labels.

items.q: Can I wash in hot water with Just 7?
items.a: Yes, if your fabric allows it. Use hot for things like towels and bedding when the label says it's fine.

items.q: Does Just 7 dissolve in cold water?
items.a: It's designed to dissolve in warm or cold water.† For very cold washes, tear it in half and don't overstuff. Cold-water guide.

items.q: Why didn't my sheet dissolve?
items.a: Usually an overstuffed drum, very cold water or a very short cycle. Tear the sheet in half, put it in first and leave room for clothes to move.

items.q: What if I find a bit of sheet on my clothes?
items.a: Rewash the item, or rinse it under warm water. Next time put the sheet in first and load less.

items.q: Can I dissolve the sheet in water first?
items.a: Yes. For very cold or quick washes, dissolve it in a cup of warm water and pour it into the drum.

items.q: Does Just 7 work on a quick wash cycle?
items.a: Yes for lightly soiled loads. Tear the sheet in half and dissolve it in warm water first for very short cycles.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 on a delicate cycle?
items.a: Yes. Use half a sheet for a small delicate load and follow care labels.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 on a heavy duty cycle?
items.a: Yes. Use two sheets for big or very dirty loads.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 on a bulky or bedding cycle?
items.a: Yes. Use one or two sheets depending on size and soil.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with a steam cycle?
items.a: Yes, if your washer's steam cycle adds detergent at the start. Follow your washer manual.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with the sanitize cycle?
items.a: Yes, if your fabrics can take it. Just 7 itself doesn't sanitize.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 on an eco or water-saving cycle?
items.a: Yes. Leave room in the drum so clothes can move.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with a prewash?
items.a: Put the sheet in the drum at the start. If you want detergent in both stages, use a half sheet dissolved in warm water in the prewash.

items.q: Do I need an extra rinse?
items.a: Usually not. Add one for very heavy loads, sensitive skin or if you used two sheets. Extra rinse explained.

items.q: Can I hand-wash with Just 7?
items.a: Yes. Dissolve a sheet or half in warm water in the sink first, then add clothes, soak, rinse and dry. Hand-wash guide.

items.q: How do I hand-wash in a sink?
items.a: Fill the sink with warm water, dissolve half a sheet, swish clothes, soak 15 to 30 minutes, then rinse until the water runs clear.

items.q: How do I hand-wash in a bucket?
items.a: Dissolve half a sheet in warm water, add clothes, agitate, soak, then rinse in clean water.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a bathtub?
items.a: Yes, for big items like comforters. Dissolve a sheet in warm water first and rinse well.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 for travel?
items.a: Yes. Sheets are light, flat and don't spill. Travel and camping guide.

items.q: Can I take laundry sheets on a plane?
items.a: They're dry, not liquid, so they're not limited like liquids. Check current rules with your airline and TSA before you fly.

items.q: How many sheets should I pack for a trip?
items.a: One half sheet per sink wash, and one sheet per machine load. A few sheets in a zip bag cover most trips.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 while camping?
items.a: Yes, for hand washing. Rinse away from lakes and streams and follow local rules for greywater.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in an RV or van?
items.a: Yes. It's compact and easy to dose. Laundry in an RV or van.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 at a laundromat?
items.a: Yes. Bring sheets in a zip bag and drop one in before your clothes. Laundromat tips.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a shared building laundry room?
items.a: Yes. Sheets are easy to carry and there's no jug to leave behind.

items.q: Can I pretreat stains with a sheet?
items.a: Wet the stain, rub a small piece of sheet into it, let it sit a few minutes, then wash.†

items.q: How do I make a pretreat paste from a sheet?
items.a: Dissolve a small piece in a few drops of warm water and work it into the stain with your fingers.

items.q: Can I soak clothes with Just 7?
items.a: Yes. Dissolve half a sheet in a basin of warm water and soak for up to a few hours, then wash.

items.q: How should I store laundry sheets?
items.a: Keep the pouch sealed and dry, away from steam and humidity, and out of reach of kids and pets. Storage tips.

items.q: Why are my sheets sticking together?
items.a: Humidity. Keep the pouch sealed and away from steam. Separate them gently with dry hands.

items.q: Can I touch the sheets with wet hands?
items.a: Try not to. Damp hands soften the film. Grab one with dry hands and reseal the pouch.

items.q: Do laundry sheets expire?
items.a: We'll print a best-by guide on the pouch once our manufacturer confirms it. Stored sealed and dry, sheets keep well.

items.q: How long does a pouch last?
items.a: Up to 60 loads. At five loads a week, that's about three months.†

items.q: Should I store the pouch in the laundry room?
items.a: Yes, if it's dry. Keep it away from the dryer vent, steam and the floor near the washer.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with fabric softener?
items.a: Yes. Add softener as usual in its own compartment. Or skip it. Do you need softener?.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with dryer sheets?
items.a: Yes. They go in the dryer and don't interact with Just 7. Are dryer sheets worth it?.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with wool dryer balls?
items.a: Yes. Do wool dryer balls work?.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with oxygen bleach?
items.a: Yes. Add it as directed on its label for whites and tough stains.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with chlorine bleach?
items.a: You can add bleach as directed on its label in your washer's bleach compartment. Never mix bleach with other cleaners outside the wash.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with vinegar?
items.a: Don't add vinegar in the same wash: acid works against washing soda. If you like vinegar, use it in the rinse compartment.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with baking soda?
items.a: Yes, though Just 7 already includes washing soda and sodium citrate to help.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with a laundry booster?
items.a: Yes. Add boosters as their labels direct.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with scent beads?
items.a: You can, but your laundry won't be fragrance-free anymore.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with a stain remover?
items.a: Yes. Pretreat with your stain remover, then wash with Just 7.

items.q: Can I mix Just 7 with my old detergent?
items.a: You can use up your old detergent first, but don't double up in one load. Use one or the other.

items.q: How do I switch from liquid detergent to sheets?
items.a: Replace a capful with one sheet for a regular load. Put it in the drum, not the dispenser.

items.q: How do I switch from pods to sheets?
items.a: One pod usually becomes one sheet for a regular load. Tear in half for small loads.

items.q: How do I switch from powder to sheets?
items.a: Replace a scoop with one sheet for a regular load, placed in the drum first.

items.q: Should I clean my washer before switching?
items.a: It's a good idea every month anyway. How to clean your washer.

items.q: How often should I wash my sheets and bedding?
items.a: Most people aim for weekly. How often to wash sheets.

items.q: Do I need to sort laundry with Just 7?
items.a: Sort as you normally would by color and fabric. When you can skip sorting.

items.q: Can kids use laundry sheets?
items.a: Older kids can, with supervision. Keep the pouch out of reach of young kids. Teaching kids laundry.

items.q: Are laundry sheets easier for people with limited grip?
items.a: Many people find a flat sheet easier than lifting a jug or measuring liquid.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 to clean other things around the house?
items.a: Just 7 is made and labeled for laundry. Use it for laundry only.

items.q: Can I wash dishes with Just 7?
items.a: No. It's a laundry detergent, not dish soap, and not for dishwashers.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a dishwasher?
items.a: No. It's for washing machines and hand-washing laundry only.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 as a body or hand soap?
items.a: No. It's laundry detergent. Use it for laundry only.

items.q: Can I mop floors with Just 7?
items.a: It isn't made or tested for floors, so we don't recommend it.

items.q: What if a sheet gets wet in the pouch?
items.a: Use or discard the damp sheet and dry the pouch before resealing. Keep the rest away from moisture.

items.q: Can I wash just one item with a sheet?
items.a: Yes. Use a quarter or half sheet, or hand-wash it in the sink.

items.q: Should I use more sheets for front loaders?
items.a: No. Same dose for every washer: half, one or two sheets by load size.

items.q: How long should a wash cycle be?
items.a: Any normal cycle works. For very short cycles, dissolve the sheet first.

items.q: Can I line dry clothes washed with Just 7?
items.a: Yes. Line drying 101.

items.q: Why do my clothes feel stiff after washing?
items.a: Often hard water or too much detergent. Use the right dose and check our hard water guide.

items.q: How do I make laundry day faster?
items.a: Fewer steps help: no measuring, one sheet, done. The 20-minute laundry week.

items.q: How do I fold laundry faster?
items.a: Fold straight from the dryer and sort by person as you go. Folding tips.

items.q: How do I make laundry less boring?
items.a: Podcast, timer, and one sheet so there's no measuring. More ideas.

items.q: What's a good laundry routine for a big family?
items.a: Small daily loads beat a weekend marathon. Big family routine.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a laundry service or wash-and-fold?
items.a: If they let you bring your own detergent, yes. Ask them first.

items.q: Do laundry sheets work in a washing bag?
items.a: Yes. Put the sheet in the drum, not inside the mesh bag.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with a pre-wash stain spray?
items.a: Yes. Spray, wait as the spray directs, then wash with Just 7.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 to wash clothes in a sink while traveling?
items.a: Yes. Half a sheet in warm sink water does a few items. Rinse well and roll in a towel to dry.

items.q: Do laundry sheets work in cold water washes on quick cycles?
items.a: Yes, with a tip: tear the sheet and dissolve it in a cup of warm water first.

items.q: How do I wash clothes when someone in the house is sick?
items.a: Wash their bedding and towels separately on the warmest setting the labels allow, and dry fully. Just 7 is a detergent, not a disinfectant.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in a hand-crank or manual washer?
items.a: Yes. Dissolve half a sheet in warm water first, then add clothes.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a travel wash bag?
items.a: Yes. Add half a sheet, warm water and clothes, then knead and rinse.

items.q: Can I pre-soak a whole load in my washer?
items.a: Yes. Start the washer with a sheet, let it fill, pause for up to an hour, then finish the cycle.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in HE washers?
items.a: Yes, it's made for HE and standard washers. The glucoside cleaners are low-sudsing, which is what HE machines want.† HE guide.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in standard washers?
items.a: Yes. Same dose, sheet in the drum first.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in top loaders?
items.a: Yes. Put the sheet in the empty drum, then clothes.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in front loaders?
items.a: Yes. Put the sheet at the back of the empty drum, then clothes.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in top loaders with an agitator?
items.a: Yes. Drop the sheet into the drum around the agitator before adding clothes.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in impeller top loaders?
items.a: Yes. Sheet on the bottom first, clothes on top.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in washer-dryer combos?
items.a: Yes. Put the sheet in the drum, not the dispenser.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in portable washers?
items.a: Yes. Use half a sheet, and dissolve it in warm water first for small, quick machines.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in compact or apartment washers?
items.a: Yes. Loads are smaller, so half a sheet is often enough.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in a twin tub washer?
items.a: Yes. Dissolve the sheet in the wash tub water before adding clothes.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in stacked washers?
items.a: Yes. Stacked units are standard front or top loaders, so dose the same way.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in Samsung, LG, Whirlpool or other brands?
items.a: Just 7 isn't made for one brand: it goes in the drum of any HE or standard washer. Follow your manual for the cycle.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in Speed Queen washers?
items.a: Yes. Speed Queens are standard top or front loaders, so put the sheet in the drum first.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in Miele or Bosch washers?
items.a: Yes. Put the sheet in the drum, not the dispenser, and skip any auto-dosing feature.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 with auto-dosing washers?
items.a: Not in the auto-dose tank: it's for liquids. Put a sheet in the drum and turn auto-dosing off for that load.

items.q: Does Just 7 work in coin laundromat machines?
items.a: Yes. Drop the sheet in the drum before your clothes.

items.q: Does Just 7 make a lot of suds?
items.a: No. Its glucoside cleaners are low-sudsing. Suds don't equal cleaning.

items.q: Why are there no suds?
items.a: Low suds is normal and what HE washers want. Clean laundry doesn't need foam.

items.q: Can sheets clog my washer?
items.a: A sheet placed in the drum first is designed to dissolve in the wash.† Don't put sheets in the dispenser drawer.

items.q: Can laundry sheets clog drains?
items.a: Just 7 is designed to dissolve in the wash.† Don't put undissolved bits down a sink.

items.q: Is Just 7 OK for septic systems?
items.a: We haven't tested that yet, so we're not claiming it. We'll update this answer when we have data.

items.q: Is Just 7 greywater safe?
items.a: We haven't tested that, so we don't claim it. Follow your local greywater rules.

items.q: What about hard water?
items.a: Two of our seven ingredients, sodium citrate and washing soda, are there for exactly that. They grab minerals so the cleaners can work.

items.q: Do I need more sheets for hard water?
items.a: Try one sheet first. For very hard water and dirty loads, step up to the next dose.

items.q: How do I know if I have hard water?
items.a: Signs include spots on glasses, crusty faucets and stiff, dull laundry. Your water utility can tell you the hardness.

items.q: Why do clothes feel stiff in hard water?
items.a: Minerals bind to detergent and fabric. Hard water fixes.

items.q: Does Just 7 work with well water?
items.a: Yes. Well water is often hard, which is why we include two water softeners.

items.q: Does Just 7 work with soft water?
items.a: Yes. In very soft water, half a sheet may be enough for light loads.

items.q: Will Just 7 leave residue in my washer?
items.a: Not when dosed right. Overdosing and overloading are the usual causes of residue.

items.q: Why does my washer smell?
items.a: Usually trapped moisture and buildup. Leave the door open after washes and clean the gasket. Washer smell fixes.

items.q: How do I clean my washing machine?
items.a: Run a hot empty cycle with a washer cleaner, wipe the gasket and dispenser, and leave the door open to dry. Full guide.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 to clean my washer?
items.a: No. Use a product made for washer cleaning.

items.q: Will Just 7 void my washer warranty?
items.a: We can't speak for washer makers. Most ask for HE-compatible, low-sudsing detergent, which Just 7 is designed to be.†

items.q: How much water does a load of laundry use?
items.a: It varies a lot by machine. HE washers use far less than older top loaders. Water per load.

items.q: How can I save water on laundry day?
items.a: Full loads, the right cycle and skipping needless rewashes. Water-saving tips.

items.q: Does cold water save energy?
items.a: Yes, heating water is a big part of a wash's energy use. Cold-water washing.

items.q: Is washing in cold water enough?
items.a: For everyday loads, often yes. Use warm or hot for heavy soil if the care label allows.

items.q: Can I use Just 7 in a dryer?
items.a: No. It's a washer detergent. Never put sheets in the dryer.

items.q: Does Just 7 work with a water softener system?
items.a: Yes. In softened water, start with the standard dose and adjust down for light loads.

items.q: Does Just 7 work at high altitude?
items.a: Yes. Altitude doesn't change how you dose a laundry sheet.

items.q: Why did my washer leave white spots on clothes?
items.a: Usually hard-water minerals or undissolved detergent from an overloaded drum. Load less and put the sheet in first.

items.q: Does the sheet need agitation to dissolve?
items.a: Movement helps. Leave room in the drum so water and clothes can move.

items.q: Is Just 7 safe for my washer's rubber seals?
items.a: Just 7 is a normal low-sudsing laundry detergent made for HE and standard washers.† Wipe gaskets regularly as your manual suggests.

items.q: What water temperature counts as cold?
items.a: Washers vary, but cold is usually around 60 to 80°F. Very cold water below that can slow dissolving.

items.q: How do I wash in very cold winter water?
items.a: Tear the sheet in half, put it in first, use a slightly warmer setting if you can, and don't overstuff.

items.q: Does Just 7 remove tough stains?
items.a: It's made for everyday loads. For heavy protein, food or set-in stains, pretreat first. Just 9, with enzymes, is planned for tough messes.

items.q: What's the best way to treat stains with Just 7?
items.a: Act fast, blot don't rub, rinse from the back with cold water, pretreat, then wash. Stain rescue cheat sheet.

items.q: Should I use hot or cold water on stains?
items.a: Cold for protein stains like blood, egg and dairy, since heat can set them. Warm helps with grease once pretreated.

items.q: Why shouldn't I put stained clothes in the dryer?
items.a: Heat can set stains. Air-dry and check before you machine-dry.

items.q: What is a protein stain?
items.a: Stains from blood, sweat, egg, dairy, baby formula and grass. Enzymes help most with these, so pretreat when using Just 7.

items.q: How do I get blood out with Just 7?
items.a: Rinse with cold water from the back, pretreat with a wet piece of sheet, soak in cold, then wash cold. Blood stain guide.

items.q: How do I get period blood out of underwear and sheets?
items.a: Cold rinse right away, pretreat, soak in cold water and wash cold. Never use hot water first.

items.q: How do I get grease and oil stains out?
items.a: Blot, sprinkle cornstarch to absorb, then work a damp piece of sheet in and wash warm if the fabric allows. Grease stain guide.

items.q: How do I get cooking oil out of a shirt?
items.a: Blot, pretreat with a wet piece of sheet, let sit 10 minutes, then wash in the warmest water the label allows.

items.q: How do I get red wine out?
items.a: Blot, flush with cold water from the back, pretreat, and wash. Skip the salt myth. Red wine guide.

items.q: How do I get coffee stains out?
items.a: Flush with cold water, pretreat, and wash. Older coffee stains may need oxygen bleach on whites. Coffee stain guide.

items.q: How do I get tea stains out?
items.a: Rinse cold from the back, pretreat with a damp piece of sheet, and wash. Oxygen bleach helps on whites.

items.q: How do I get grass stains out?
items.a: Pretreat with a damp piece of sheet, soak in cool water, and wash. Grass stain guide.

items.q: How do I get mud out?
items.a: Let it dry, brush off what you can, then pretreat and wash. Mud guide.

items.q: How do I get ink out of a shirt?
items.a: Dab with rubbing alcohol on a cloth, blot, then pretreat and wash. Ink guide.

items.q: How do I get makeup out of a collar?
items.a: Pretreat foundation with a damp piece of sheet, let sit, then wash. Makeup stain guide.

items.q: How do I get lipstick out?
items.a: Scrape off excess, dab with rubbing alcohol, pretreat and wash. Test on a hidden spot first.

items.q: How do I get foundation out of clothes?
items.a: Pretreat with a damp piece of sheet, work it in gently and wash.

items.q: How do I get mascara out of a pillowcase?
items.a: Dab with a little rubbing alcohol or makeup remover, then pretreat and wash.

items.q: How do I get chocolate out?
items.a: Scrape off excess, rinse cold from the back, pretreat and wash. Chocolate guide.

items.q: How do I get tomato sauce or ketchup out?
items.a: Scrape, rinse cold from the back, pretreat and wash. Sunlight can fade the last bit. Tomato stain guide.

items.q: How do I get spaghetti sauce out of a white shirt?
items.a: Rinse cold from the back, pretreat, wash, and line-dry in the sun. Repeat before machine drying.

items.q: How do I get yellow armpit stains out?
items.a: Pretreat with a paste of a damp sheet piece, soak, and wash. Oxygen bleach helps on whites. Armpit stain guide.

items.q: How do I get deodorant marks out?
items.a: Rub fabric against itself to lift fresh marks. For buildup, pretreat and soak before washing.

items.q: How do I get sweat stains out?
items.a: Rinse, pretreat, soak in cool water and wash. Wash workout clothes soon after wearing.

items.q: How do I get sunscreen stains out?
items.a: Treat like grease: pretreat, let sit, and wash warm if the fabric allows. Sunscreen stain guide.

items.q: How do I get baby food stains out?
items.a: Scrape, rinse cold, pretreat and wash. Baby food and formula stains.

items.q: How do I get formula and spit-up stains out?
items.a: Rinse cold right away, pretreat, and wash. These are protein stains, so avoid hot water first.

items.q: How do I get breast milk stains out?
items.a: Rinse with cold water, pretreat and wash cold. It's a protein stain.

items.q: How do I get poop stains out of baby clothes?
items.a: Rinse off solids with cold water, pretreat, soak, and wash. Sunlight can fade leftover marks on whites.

items.q: How do I get pet urine out of bedding?
items.a: Rinse with cold water, wash, and air-dry to check before machine drying. Pet accident guide.

items.q: How do I get vomit out of clothes?
items.a: Remove solids, rinse cold, pretreat and wash. Repeat before drying if needed.

items.q: How do I get candle wax out of fabric?
items.a: Freeze it, scrape it off, then press with paper towels and a warm iron, and wash. Holiday stains guide.

items.q: How do I get gravy out of a tablecloth?
items.a: Scrape, blot, pretreat as a grease stain, and wash in the warmest water the fabric allows.

items.q: How do I get butter stains out?
items.a: Treat as grease: blot, pretreat, let sit, and wash warm if allowed.

items.q: How do I get salad dressing out?
items.a: Blot, pretreat as an oil stain, and wash warm if the fabric allows.

items.q: How do I get berry stains out?
items.a: Flush with cold water from the back, pretreat and wash. Sunlight can help fade leftovers.

items.q: How do I get mustard out?
items.a: Scrape, flush cold, pretreat, and wash. Mustard can be stubborn, so repeat before drying.

items.q: How do I get curry or turmeric stains out?
items.a: Scrape, rinse cold, pretreat and wash, then dry in sunlight to help fade it.

items.q: How do I get juice stains out?
items.a: Rinse with cold water, pretreat and wash.

items.q: How do I get soda stains out?
items.a: Rinse cold, pretreat and wash. Sugary stains rinse out well if treated fast.

items.q: How do I get ice cream out?
items.a: Rinse cold, pretreat and wash cold. It's dairy, so heat can set it.

items.q: How do I get egg stains out?
items.a: Scrape, rinse with cold water, pretreat and wash cold. Hot water can cook the egg into the fabric.

items.q: How do I get rust stains out?
items.a: Rust needs a dedicated rust remover. Follow its label before washing with Just 7.

items.q: How do I get paint out of clothes?
items.a: Water-based paint: rinse while wet and wash. Oil paint needs a solvent first. Dried paint may be permanent.

items.q: How do I get slime or glue out?
items.a: Scrape what you can, soak in warm water to soften, pretreat and wash.

items.q: How do I get gum off clothes?
items.a: Freeze it, scrape it off, then pretreat any residue and wash.

items.q: How do I get pen marks off a couch cover?
items.a: Check the care label, dab with rubbing alcohol, blot, then wash if the cover is washable.

items.q: How do I get motor oil out?

items.q: How are laundry detergent sheets made?
items.a: Ingredients are mixed into a liquid, spread thin, dried into a film and cut into sheets. Most of the water dries off.

items.q: How do detergent sheets work?
items.a: The film dissolves in the wash and releases the cleaners and water softeners, just like a liquid would.

items.q: What do laundry sheets do?
items.a: They clean clothes, the same job as liquid or powder detergent, in a dry pre-measured sheet.

items.q: Are laundry sheets safe?
items.a: We don't make safety claims. Use as directed and store any detergent away from kids and pets.

items.q: Are laundry sheets toxic?
items.a: "Toxic" depends on dose and exposure, and any detergent can harm if eaten. Store sheets out of reach and read the full ingredient list.

items.q: Are laundry sheets bad for you?
items.a: We don't make health claims. You can check all seven of our ingredients on our ingredients page.

items.q: Are laundry sheets bad for your washer?
items.a: Used as directed, no. Put the sheet in the drum, not the dispenser, and don't overload.

items.q: Do laundry sheets dissolve completely?
items.a: Just 7 is designed to dissolve fully in the wash.† Overloading and very cold, short cycles are the usual culprits when bits remain.

items.q: Which laundry sheets dissolve the best?
items.a: It varies by formula. We're publishing our own cold-water dissolving test for Just 7.†

items.q: When should I use laundry sheets?
items.a: Any everyday wash: clothes, sheets, towels, pet bedding. Pretreat heavy stains.

items.q: Why use detergent sheets?
items.a: No jug, no measuring, no drips, light to carry and easy to store.

items.q: Why are laundry sheets bad, according to critics?
items.a: Critics point to weaker performance on tough stains in some tests and debates over PVA film. We answer both: pretreat heavy stains, and we use pullulan instead of PVA.†

items.q: Do laundry sheets contain plastic?
items.a: Many use PVA film. Just 7 uses pullulan.†

items.q: Do laundry sheets have microplastics?
items.a: It depends on the film. Ours is pullulan, designed to dissolve in the wash.†

items.q: What laundry sheets are plastic-free?
items.a: Look for a non-PVA film and confirmed packaging. Just 7 is plastic-free by design; we're confirming it in writing.†

items.q: Where are laundry detergent sheets made?
items.a: It varies by brand. We'll state where Just 7 is made on the pouch before launch.

items.q: Are laundry sheets made in the USA?
items.a: Some are. We'll confirm Just 7's country of origin on the pouch before launch.

items.q: What laundry sheets are made in Canada or the UK?
items.a: We can't speak for every brand. We'll state where Just 7 is made before launch.

items.q: Where can I buy laundry sheets?
items.a: Just 7 is on just7sheets.com. Pre-order now. Orders ship Jan 11th.

items.q: Are laundry sheets perforated?
items.a: Just 7 sheets tear cleanly in half by hand for small loads.

items.q: Do laundry sheets stick together?
items.a: They can in humid air. Keep the pouch sealed and handle with dry hands.

items.q: Do laundry sheets work for heavily soiled clothes?
items.a: Use two sheets and pretreat. For heavy protein stains, Just 9 is planned.

items.q: Do laundry sheets need fabric softener?
items.a: No. Softener is optional.

items.q: Are laundry sheets good for towels?
items.a: Yes. Use one sheet, skip softener and dry fully.

items.q: Are laundry sheets good for whites?
items.a: Yes for everyday whites. Add oxygen bleach for tough stains.

items.q: Can laundry sheets cause skin irritation?
items.a: Any detergent can bother some people. Just 7 skips fragrance and dyes, and an extra rinse helps if you're sensitive.

items.q: How long do laundry sheets last once opened?
items.a: Many months if the pouch stays sealed and dry between uses.

items.q: Can laundry sheets get wet before use?
items.a: Avoid it. Moisture softens the film and makes sheets stick.

items.q: Can I use a laundry sheet that got damp?
items.a: Yes, use it in the next wash.

items.q: How many sheets per load for a king comforter?
items.a: Two sheets, on a bulky cycle with an extra rinse.

items.q: How many sheets for a load of towels?
items.a: One sheet for a regular load of towels, two for a full drum.

items.q: How many loads does one sheet do?
items.a: One sheet does one regular load. Half a sheet does a small load.

items.q: Are laundry sheets good value?
items.a: Compare per load: Just 7 is about $0.25 a load with subscribe and save.†

items.q: Why are some laundry sheets scented?
items.a: Brands add fragrance for scent. Just 7 adds none.

items.q: Do laundry sheets smell good?
items.a: Scented ones do; Just 7 has no smell at all.

items.q: Are laundry sheets good for the environment?
items.a: They cut jug waste and shipping weight. The film and packaging matter too. Honest look.

items.q: Do laundry sheets work as well as liquid detergent on everyday dirt?
items.a: For everyday loads, sheets do the job for most people. We're running a side-by-side test before making any claim.†

items.q: How do I know laundry sheets are working?
items.a: Clothes come out clean and smell like nothing. If a smell remains, rewash with the next dose up.

items.q: Can I use laundry sheets for delicates?
items.a: Yes. Half a sheet, cold water, delicate cycle or hand wash.

items.q: Why do laundry sheets cost more than store brand liquid?
items.a: Sometimes they don't. Compare cost per load at your real dose.

items.q: What's the best laundry sheet?
items.a: The one whose label you're happy with. Compare ingredients, film and cost per load. Just 7 is built for a short label.

items.q: Can laundry sheets damage clothes?
items.a: Used as directed, Just 7 is a normal laundry detergent with no bleach. Follow care labels.

items.q: Why do my clothes smell musty after washing?
items.a: Usually they sat wet too long or didn't dry fully. Move clothes to the dryer right away and clean your washer gasket.

items.q: Why do my clothes smell bad after drying?
items.a: Often a dirty lint trap, damp loads or buildup in the washer. Clean both machines and don't overload.

items.q: Why do my clothes smell sour after washing?
items.a: Bacteria grow when wet laundry sits. Rewash and dry right away.

items.q: Why do my clothes smell like mildew?
items.a: Damp storage or slow drying. Rewash with an extra rinse and dry fully.

items.q: Why do my clothes smell burnt after drying?
items.a: Check for lint buildup in the dryer and vent, and have it serviced if the smell continues.

items.q: Why do my clothes shrink when I wash them?
items.a: Heat and agitation. Use cold water, gentler cycles and lower dryer heat.

items.q: How do I get rid of static in clothes?
items.a: Don't overdry, separate synthetics, or try dryer balls.

items.q: How do I stop clothes from pilling?
items.a: Wash inside out, use gentle cycles, and avoid washing with rough items like jeans.

items.q: How do I get rid of clothes moths?
items.a: Wash or freeze affected items, vacuum closets, and store wool clean and sealed.

items.q: How do I get odor out of clothes?
items.a: Wash promptly, don't overload, dry fully, and add an extra rinse if needed.

items.q: Should I wash new sheets before using them?
items.a: Yes. Washing removes finishes from manufacturing.

items.q: Should I wash new clothes before wearing them?
items.a: It's a good habit, especially for baby clothes and anything worn close to the skin.

items.q: Can I wash sheets and towels together?
items.a: You can, but towels shed lint on sheets. Separate loads keep both nicer.

items.q: Can I wash sheets with clothes?
items.a: Yes, if colors and temperatures match. Big sheets can tangle smaller items.

items.q: Is laundry detergent the same as soap?
items.a: No. Detergents are made to work in hard water without leaving soap scum.

items.q: Is laundry detergent the same as fabric softener?
items.a: No. Detergent cleans; softener coats fabric to feel soft.

items.q: Does laundry detergent kill germs?
items.a: Detergent removes dirt and many germs with water and agitation, but it isn't a disinfectant. Just 7 makes no germ claims.

items.q: Does laundry detergent go bad?
items.a: Liquids can separate over time. Dry sheets keep well sealed and dry.

items.q: Does laundry detergent freeze?
items.a: Liquids can. Dry sheets aren't affected by cold.

items.q: Is laundry detergent flammable?
items.a: Detergent isn't typically considered flammable, but store any cleaning product away from heat.

items.q: Why is laundry detergent blue?
items.a: Dyes are added for looks. Just 7 has no dyes.

items.q: Is laundry detergent HSA eligible?
items.a: Generally no. Check with your plan administrator.

items.q: Can I wash clothes without detergent?
items.a: Water alone removes some dirt, but detergent is what lifts oil and grime.

items.q: How much detergent do I really need?
items.a: Less than most people use. Overdosing causes residue.

items.q: Should I use fabric softener on towels?
items.a: Skip it. Softener can reduce absorbency.

items.q: Are dryer sheets necessary?
items.a: No. Many people skip them. Dryer sheets: worth it?.

items.q: Are dryer sheets bad for you?
items.a: We don't make health claims about other products. Just 7 is a washer detergent, not a dryer sheet.

items.q: Do dryer sheets remove pet hair?
items.a: Some people say they help loosen hair. A no-heat tumble and lint roller help too.

items.q: Do dryer sheets keep mice or bugs away?
items.a: That's a popular tip, but it isn't something we can vouch for.

items.q: Can dryer sheets be reused?
items.a: Usually they lose effect after one use. Dryer balls are reusable.

items.q: What laundry cycle should I use?
items.a: Normal for most loads, delicate for fragile items, heavy duty for very dirty ones.

items.q: How often should I wash towels?
items.a: About every three or four uses, and dry fully between uses.

items.q: How often should I wash jeans?
items.a: Less often than you think. Jeans guide.

items.q: How often should I wash pillows?
items.a: Every few months, plus pillowcases weekly. Pillow guide.

items.q: How often should I wash bras?
items.a: Every few wears. Hand-wash or use a mesh bag.

items.q: How often should I wash pajamas?
items.a: Every few wears, or more if you sweat at night.

items.q: How often should I clean my washer?
items.a: About once a month.

items.q: How often should I clean my dryer vent?
items.a: At least once a year, plus the lint trap every load.

items.q: How do I wash clothes faster?
items.a: Run small loads more often, and use one sheet with no measuring.

items.q: How do I keep black clothes black?
items.a: Inside out, cold water, gentle cycle, and line dry.

items.q: How do I wash clothes so they last longer?
items.a: Wash less often, use cold water, turn inside out and air-dry.

items.q: How do I do laundry in a small apartment?
items.a: Use a drying rack and compact supplies. Small-space laundry.

items.q: How do I do laundry for spring cleaning?
items.a: Wash winter bedding, curtains and pillows. Spring laundry reset.

items.q: How do I wash clothes after gardening?
items.a: Shake off soil outside first, then pretreat and wash. Gardeners' guide.

items.q: How do I wash clothes in a hotel sink?
items.a: Plug the sink, dissolve half a sheet in warm water, wash, rinse and roll in a towel to dry.

items.q: How do I air-dry clothes indoors?
items.a: Use a rack near airflow, space items out, and avoid damp rooms.

items.q: What's the best way to dry clothes to save energy?
items.a: Line dry when you can. Line drying 101.

items.q: Should I wash clothes inside out?
items.a: Yes for darks, prints and activewear: it protects color and the outer surface.

items.q: Should I zip zippers before washing?
items.a: Yes. It prevents snags on other clothes.

items.q: Should I separate lights and darks?
items.a: Yes, especially for new or bright colors.

items.q: Can I wash red and white clothes together?
items.a: Not with new reds. Wash them separately in cold until they stop bleeding.

items.q: What is a laundry routine for busy people?
items.a: Small loads on set days. 20-minute laundry week.

items.q: How do I wash flannel and wool in fall?
items.a: Cool water and gentle cycles. Fall laundry guide.

items.q: What laundry products do I actually need?
items.a: A detergent, a stain plan, and maybe oxygen bleach. Most other products are optional.

items.q: Do I need a separate stain remover?
items.a: For tough stains, it helps. For everyday spots, a damp piece of sheet works as a pretreat.

items.q: Why are my clothes still dirty after washing?
items.a: Overloading, too little detergent or set-in stains. Load less, use the right dose and pretreat.

items.q: Why do my towels smell after one use?
items.a: Bacteria from buildup. Wash hot if allowed without softener and dry fully.

items.q: Is it OK to leave clothes in the washer overnight?
items.a: Try not to. Damp clothes can sour. Rewash if they smell.

items.q: How do I remove detergent buildup from clothes?
items.a: Run a hot or warm wash with no detergent, or an extra rinse, and use less going forward.

items.q: How do I strip laundry?
items.a: Some people soak items in hot water with boosters to remove buildup. Follow care labels, and check with diaper makers before stripping cloth diapers.

items.q: Can I wash shoes in a washing machine?
items.a: Many canvas shoes, yes, on gentle in a bag. Skip leather.

items.q: How do I wash farm or barn clothes?
items.a: Shake off dirt and hair outside, pretreat, and wash separately with two sheets.
